name: Hashishene

papers.title: Multidimensional analysis of cannabis volatile constituents: identification of 5,5-dimethyl-1-vinylbicyclo[2.1.1]hexane as a volatile marker of hashish, the resin of Cannabis sativa L

research.basis: MeSH indexing and publication types of the most relevant PubMed records; counts are of papers in the sample, not findings.

vocabulary.structure: SEPIO assertion / evidence line / evidence item

evidence: Measured in 3 of 6 MONDAYS hemp SKUs at 0.24–0.37% of total volatiles (0.048–0.074mg per chew).

consumer_summary.what_it_is: Hashishene is a volatile monoterpene that helps give hashish its distinctive aroma. Chemically known as 5,5-dimethyl-1-vinylbicyclo[2.1.1]hexane, it is a unique scent molecule created when plant material undergoes light exposure and oxidation. A person is most likely to encounter it in the scent of aged or processed cannabis resin.
consumer_summary.found_in: It has been identified as a specific volatile marker in the resin of Cannabis sativa L.
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Researchers are drawn to hashishene because it serves as a unique chemical fingerprint for hashish. By studying the photochemical processes and oxidation-reduction reactions that create it, analytical chemists can better understand how plant resins age and transform over time. The current literature consists of analytical chemistry profiling (Oxford level 5).
consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: The available research is limited to a single analytical chemistry study (Oxford level 5) identifying it as a volatile marker in cannabis resin.
